mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2% and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 4% and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals a weakening supply chain, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate concerns about economic health.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines > 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 6% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines for 2 months, but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2%, but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% MoM and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% YoY and industrial production (INDPRO) declines, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < 1% and INDPRO MoM decline
failure_condition: If GDPC1 YoY growth < 1% and INDPRO declines, but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.
